gen-dafont-outrun-future-fs-hoover: Hoover is a sturdy serif with short ascenders and a generous opening into the e. Outrun Future sits above it with wide-spaced, outline-like letters of constant width, and a long read stays comfortable because the body keeps its lines compact and refined.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab is a dignified serif whose caps sit almost level with its lowercase. And Outrun Future, wide-spaced with a ring-like o of constant wall, gives way to it so a long stretch of text feels dense, steady and refined.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-literata: Bookish and sophisticated, Literata is the quiet half, with curved letters that open their mouths wide. Over There, in a fixed-nib vintage-military hand with generous gaps between glyphs, leads; Literata then carries a long stretch of reading with sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones.
gen-dafont-over-there-fs-sentient: Letters that look drawn by a fixed-width nib give Over There its command. It is built for loud, spacious headings, while Sentient, a contemporary text serif with pinched apertures and thinner crossbars, does the patient work of carrying words.
gen-dafont-quantum-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab reads grounded and refined, its tall lowercase filling each line. Quantum, loose and bent-paperclip-like with no swelling, earns its keep in big, short headings where all that breathing space can show.
gen-dafont-redux-fs-bespoke-slab: Grounded and geometric together, this pair pulls a wide-set heading toward a tall-bodied serif. And Redux, with its visible curve entrances and moderate thick-thin shift, is the lively side while Bespoke Slab stays refined and low in contrast.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-fs-bespoke-sl: Striking and classic, SF Wonder Comic packs its words dense and tall, with bowls left open on one side. And Bespoke Slab, a grounded serif with tall lowercase and low contrast, gives those headings something refined to settle into.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-bespoke-slab: Huge stretches of blank space between letters make Starborn feel dreamy and weightless. But Bespoke Slab, a refined serif with tall lowercase bodies, anchors the pair, and that grounding is the thing that makes it work.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-erode: Starborn floats, scattered with open space between its letters. Erode, a text serif with a tall middle band and broad openings, is what makes the pair work, because its strokes ebb and flow gently enough to feel related to the heading.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-trench-slab: Starborn is all drifting space and one dark stripe of lowercase, dreamy and loose, against a dignified serif. Trench Slab holds the ground, and shrinking the heading would lose it.
